memory_update.text: BWXT should remain the reference public-market benchmark for advanced nuclear components and fuel fabrication, but it is already well covered and above the preferred underfollowed market-cap sweet spot.
Curtiss-Wright is a direct advanced-reactor component qualification candidate because of ASME Section III Division 5 certification for high-temperature advanced reactor and SMR metallic components.
Graham Corporation is an underfollowed second-order candidate: nuclear exposure is hidden inside naval nuclear propulsion components, heat-transfer equipment, condensers and vacuum ejectors.
Flowserve is a diversified industrial with meaningful nuclear pump, valve and seal credentials; relevance depends on proving nuclear backlog/materiality rather than installed-base marketing alone.

summary: Expanded the universe around nuclear-grade manufacturing and advanced-reactor supply-chain qualification rather than reactor developers. The strongest direct public-market anchor remains BWX Technologies, but this pass adds less obvious second-order suppliers in nuclear-qualified valves, pumps, controls, heat exchangers, condensers, sealing systems, and ASME-certified component fabrication. The underfollowed lane is most interesting where nuclear exposure is hidden inside diversified industrial or defense-manufacturing labels, especially Graham and Flowserve. Curtiss-Wright is highly relevant but now close to the upper size limit, so it is included as a direct but less underfollowed large-cap reference/discovery bridge.
